summary.headline: KDDL H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.5% YoY to Rs 1,345.8 crore, with PAT of Rs 92.9 crore at a 6.9% margin.
summary.overview: KDDL reported strong H1 FY27 top-line growth, with consolidated total income up 33.5% YoY to Rs 1,345.8 crore and Q2 up 31.6% to Rs 698.7 crore. Precision engineering (Eigen) and packaging (Ornapak) grew fastest, while the bracelet unit faced export softness linked to the Swiss watch industry. Management pulled forward Eigen capex (FY27 spend now about Rs 70-75 crore, up roughly Rs 15-20 crore from about Rs 50 crore) and said watch components growth would exceed the earlier 12-14% guidance. Consolidated PAT margin was 6.9% for both Q2 and H1, and management reiterated a 20-25% medium-term growth goal for Eigen.

segments.name: Watch components (Dials and Hands)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue grew about 30% YoY, led by volume from domestic and export customers. Management now expects FY27 growth above the original 12-14% guidance.

segments.name: Bracelet unit (100% export)
segments.commentary: Performance hit by subdued export demand and a slowdown in Swiss watch offtake. Management is adding customers in other geographies, with results expected from next quarter onwards.

segments.name: Precision engineering (Eigen)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew close to 50% YoY, driven by export demand and new customers. Medium-term goal is 20-25% CAGR; the US is about 50% of segment revenue per the analyst, and the company focuses on US, Americas and Europe.

segments.name: Packaging (Ornapak)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 30% in H1 from a low base. Q2 achieved positive PBT for the first time, with positive profitability expected to continue.

segments.name: Silver City / Luba (Swiss watch brand)
segments.commentary: Sales volumes are above management expectations and the brand sells in over 35 countries with about 45 doors outside Ethos. Management expects FY27 loss to be significantly lower than FY26 and sees possible break-even next year.

guidance_outlook: Watch components FY27 revenue growth expected above the original 12-14% guidance.
Eigen: medium-term growth goal of 20-25% CAGR maintained; management sees upside if current momentum continues.
FY27 capex now about Rs 70-75 crore (earlier about Rs 50 crore), including pulled-forward expansion that had been planned for FY28.
Unit 2B adjacent plot agreement finalised; expected to be operational mid-FY28.
Packaging expected to keep positive profitability through remaining quarters and in future years.
Silver City/Luba: FY27 loss expected to be significantly lower than FY26; possible break-even next year; budgets for next two years may be revised upward.
capex_capacity: Eigen rack plating line installed at unit 2A (new facility about 6 km from existing plant); other machines relocated there.
Eigen expansion of space at existing unit 1 to add manufacturing area.
Rack plating line commissioned; trial samples sent to customer, commercial supplies expected in one to two months.
Capex guidance for the current year about Rs 70-75 crore including pre-poning; earlier plan about Rs 50 crore. Debt will be raised to fund capex.
Management uses an approximate 3:1 revenue-to-capex norm for Eigen (not a formal guidance).
demand_pricing: Eigen demand from US and Europe; management said US RFQs slowed on tariffs but were offset by European RFQs.
Eigen new customers span energy storage (BESS), EV, electronics, aerospace and defence; the company is not focused on China or Asia.
Gross margin dipped sequentially because of mix: Eigen and export mix are growing differently, and domestic sales carry lower margin than export.
Currency impact on H1 growth was small; growth was majorly volume-driven.
Export contributes about 75% of total company sales; Eigen export share is slightly below that per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is Eigen's 50% growth due to backlog or new customers, and what is the US share and data-centre/AI exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a backlog. Funnel projects converted faster and larger than expected from existing and new customers, and the company sees no major impact from AI/data-centre capex swings given its small share.

qa_highlights.question: Which new customer sectors and capabilities were added at Eigen, and how large is the capex-linked revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: New customers span BESS, EV, electronics, aerospace and defence. Capabilities added include rack plating, welding, blanking and machining. Capex is typically sized at about a 3:1 revenue-to-capex norm; FY27 capex is about Rs 70-75 crore, up Rs 15-20 crore from the earlier Rs 50 crore plan.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix and reasons for the sequential gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company declined to give granular revenue mix. Management attributed the margin dip mainly to mix, as Eigen grows faster than watch components and domestic sales grow faster than export. Impact is described as not very significant.

qa_highlights.question: Growth in watch components and whether H2 growth can match H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Watch components grew about 30% YoY in H1, slightly below the company average because Eigen and packaging grew faster. Management said full-year watch components growth will exceed the 12-14% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Silver City/Luba unit volumes, ASPs, break-even and capital ceiling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose unit volumes or ASPs. Volumes are above expectations and footprint is over 35 countries. It hopes to break even as early as next year, and says the loss will be much lower than in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan to move into full cell-contact systems, and what are new busbar and aerospace opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay focused on its core capabilities and will invest only where they add value. Focus remains on EV and BESS; new segments may come in about five years.

risks_watch: Bracelet unit export slowdown tied to Swiss watch offtake; recovery is expected from next quarter but depends on new customer trials.
Rising debt and working capital needs from the capex pull-forward; watch for the funding mix and interest cost.
Gross margin pressure from mix shift toward lower-margin domestic and Eigen sales.
Tariff-related slowdown in US RFQs; Europe is compensating. Monitor US order flow.
Luba/Silver City losses: break-even timing is uncertain and depends on the Swiss market recovery (US, UAE and China demand).
Management declined to disclose segment-level revenue mix, ASPs and unit volumes, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Eigen and packaging, with management describing the Eigen growth as a pleasant surprise and pulling capex forward. Cautious on the bracelet unit and the Swiss watch market, and evasive on granular disclosures (revenue mix, ASPs, unit volumes, Luba capital ceiling).
key_quotes: It's not really a backlog. We are just seeing a lot of responsiveness from existing customers, new customers.
The growth has been led by volume growth, both from the domestic and export customers, which is a very healthy sign than a growth driven merely by higher realizations.

We believe there is a meaningful opportunity for high quality locally manufactured packaging solutions, particularly as brands increasingly look for supply chain responsiveness, consistent quality and shorter lead times.
